mamar.bio: A Basran transmitter who settled in Yemen.
as: ثقة ثبت فاضل إلا أن في روايته عن ثابت والأعمش وهشام بن عروة شيئا وكذا فيما حدث به بالبصرة
Trustworthy, firm and eminent, with reservations about reports from Thābit, al-Aʿmash and Hishām ibn ʿUrwah and what he narrated in Basra.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
لا أعلم اجمع لأحد غير معمر
I know of no one besides Maʿmar who combined (all six pivotal transmitters).
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان من أطلب أهل زمانه للعلم
He was among the most avid seekers of knowledge of his time.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ومعمر أثبت في الزهري من ابن عيينة
Maʿmar is more reliable on al-Zuhrī than Ibn ʿUyaynah.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Maʿmar's narration from Thābit is weak.
عمرو بن علي, quoted by al-Mizzī
Maʿmar is among the most truthful of people.
معمر بن راشد بصري سكن اليمن، ثقة، رجل صالح
Maʿmar ibn Rāshid, a Basran who settled in Yemen, trustworthy, a righteous man.
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
ومعمر ثقة، وصالح التثبت عن الزهري
Maʿmar is trustworthy and reasonably accurate from al-Zuhrī.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما حدث معمر بالبصرة فيه أغاليط، وهو صالح الحديث
What Maʿmar narrated in Basra contains errors; he is acceptable in hadith.
Maʿmar ibn Rāshid, the trustworthy, the reliable.
عليكم بهذا الرجل، يعني معمرا - فإنه لم يبق أحد من أهل زمانه أعلم منه
Hold to this man (Maʿmar), for no one of his time remains more knowledgeable than he.
He was a jurist, precise, a memoriser and scrupulous.
وكان معمر رجلا له حلم ومروءة ونبل في نفسه
Maʿmar was a man of forbearance, manly virtue and nobility of character.

t1953.bio: Ibn Ḥajar rates Rufayʿ ibn Mihrān, Abū al-ʿĀliya al-Riyāḥī, as trustworthy but frequently given to irsāl, of the second generation. He died in 90 AH, or it is said 93, or later. He is among the teachers of Muslim.
as: He is trustworthy but frequently transmits in an unattached manner (mursal).
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو القاسم اللالكائي, quoted by al-Mizzī
ذهب علم أبي العالية، لم يكن له رواة.
Abū al-ʿĀliya's learning was lost. He had no transmitters for it.
أبو بكر بن أبو داود, quoted by al-Mizzī
ليس أحد بعد الصحابة أعلم بالقران من أبي العالية
After the Companions no one knew the Qurʾān better than Abū al-ʿĀliyah.
له أحاديث صالحة وأكبر ما نقم عليه حديث الضحك في الصلاة
He has sound hadiths; the main objection to him is the hadith on laughing in prayer.
His other hadiths are sound and acceptable.
إن هذا العلم يزيد الشريف شرفا ويجلس المملوك على الأسرة
This knowledge adds honour to the noble and seats the slave on couches.
كان أبو العالية إذا اجتمع إليه أكثر من أربعة قام وتركهم
Abū al-ʿĀliya would get up and leave if more than four people assembled around him.
ابن أبو داود, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
ليس أحد بعد الصحابة أعلم بالقرآن من أبي العالية، وبعده سعيد بن جبير
After the Companions no one knew the Qurʾān better than Abū al-ʿĀliyah, then Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.
al-ʿIjlī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
A trustworthy Successor, among their senior members.
Abū Dāwūd, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
ذهب علم أبي العالية لم يكن له رواة.
Abū al-ʿĀliya's learning was lost. He had no transmitters for it.
al-ʿIjlī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
وقد وثقه العجلي، وابن حبان، وغيرهما
al-Shāfiʿī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
Al-Riyāḥī's hadith is wind (worthless) — referring to one specific hadith.
Ibn ʿAdī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
Ibn Ḥibbān, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
Ibn Ḥibbān and others declared him trustworthy.
Ibn Ḥibbān, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
He was trustworthy and transmitted many hadiths.
قد أدرك رفيع عليا ولم يسمع منه.
Rufayʿ lived in ʿAlī's time but did not hear from him.

t6291.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus al-Asadī, Abū al-Zubayr al-Makkī, as truthful but practicing tadlīs, of the fourth generation; he died in 126.
as: truthful, except that he practices tadlīs
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة صدوق وإلى الضعف ما هو
Reliable and truthful, though he tends toward weakness.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
قد احتمله الناس، وأبو الزبير أحب إلي من أبي سفيان لأن أبا الزبير أعلم بالحديث منه ، وأبو الزبير ليس به بأس
People accepted him; I prefer him to Abū Sufyān as he knew hadith better; there is no harm in him.
حدثنا أبو الزبير، وأبو الزبير أبو الزبير! قلت لأبي: كأنه يضعفه؟ قال: نعم
Ayyūb would say 'Abū al-Zubayr told us, and Abū al-Zubayr is Abū al-Zubayr!'; Aḥmad confirmed he meant to weaken him.
حدثنا أبو الزبير وهو أبو الزبير. أي كأنه يضعفه
Ibn ʿUyaynah said 'Abū al-Zubayr told us, and he is Abū al-Zubayr', as if weakening him.
Asked why he abandoned him, Shuʿbah said he saw him weighing and tipping the scale in his own favour.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Ibn Maʿīn called him sound, and once trustworthy (also trustworthy in Ibn Abī Khaythamah's report).
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Asked if he is used as proof, Abū Zurʿah said only the hadith of trustworthy men is used as proof.
وكفى بأبي الزبير صدقا أن يحدث عنه مالك، فإن مالكا لا يروي إلا عن ثقة
It suffices for his truthfulness that Mālik transmitted from him, for Mālik narrates only from trustworthy men; he is himself trustworthy.
لم ينصف من قدح فيه، لأن من استرجح في الوزن لنفسه لم يستحق الترك لأجله
Those who disparaged him were unfair; tipping a scale for oneself does not warrant abandoning a narrator.
وكان ثقة كثير الحديث إلا أن شعبة تركه لشيء زعم أنه رآه فعله في معاملة
Reliable and prolific in hadith, though Shuʿbah stopped taking from him because of something he said he saw him do in a transaction.
Abū al-Zubayr remembered the hadith best among us.
